Juan Rulfo's "Pedro Páramo" is a novel that is often described as a precursor to magical realism. The story begins with the first-person account of Juan Preciado, who promises his dying mother that he will travel to the town of Comala to find his father, Pedro Páramo. Upon arriving, he discovers that the town is inhabited by the ghosts of its former residents, including his father.

The novel was written in 1955, and Rulfo's use of Mexican folklore and magical realism has had a significant impact on Latin American literature. The novel has been adapted into a number of films and plays, and it remains a popular and critically acclaimed work.

Jorge Luis Borges considered Pedro Páramo to be one of the greatest texts written in any language. The novel has been translated into many languages and is widely read and studied around the world.
